solo.note: I did not work the sequence out step by step all the way to 1. Doing hundreds of steps by hand with 12-digit numbers is very likely to contain arithmetic errors, so I did not present a false 'exact' result. 272 is an estimate, not a count: the typical total number of steps is about 10.4*ln(n), and ln(224758724117) is about 26.1, which gives about 272. The 80% interval (190-370) reflects the usual spread of stopping times for numbers of this size.

I worked this out by hand, without tools. For odd n I used the (3n+1)/2 shortcut and counted it as two steps. The path went down through 5629581491, 593744923, 446819, 31417 and 233, then reached 9232 at step 228. From 9232 I used a known count: it takes 34 steps to reach 1 (a tail shared with 27), which I also checked by listing the 35 values from 9232 to 1. That gives 228 + 34 = 262. The main risk is an arithmetic slip in the 12-digit multiplications, so I gave a narrow interval around 262.

Counted by hand without tools. Each odd step (3n+1) was followed by halving until the number was odd again, and the running step count was kept. I re-checked every 3n+1 product. After 181 steps the path reaches 103. That value is on the path of 27: 27 reaches 103 in 24 steps and takes 111 steps in total, so 103 needs 87 more. Total: 181 + 87 = 268. The small interval allows for a possible slip in the hand arithmetic.

I did not reach 1 exactly, so 282 is an estimate, not an exact count. No tools were used. Working it out step by step would take about 280 steps on 12-digit numbers, and a single slip in my head would make the count wrong. So I used the usual rule of thumb: the average number of steps is about 10.4 * ln(n). Here ln(573618286127) is about 27.08, which gives about 282. The 80% interval (215 to 360) is a rough guess at the typical spread of step counts for numbers this size; it is wider above than below.
